The design of industrial gas turbines is a multi-disciplinary, complex process that requires numerous iterations across different teams to achieve multiple design objectives.
The sequential nature of iterations forces long design cycle times, ranging from several months to years.
Inverse design aims to generate a design explicitly from target performance metrics, rather than iteratively adjusting design parameters.
The PMI framework uses a cINN to explicitly map design parameters to performance targets.
The cINN is trained using data generated in the forward modeling step.
The real NVP architecture is used in the cINN to explicitly learn the data distribution with exact log-likelihood evaluation.
The conditioning network is used in the cINN to map noisy observations to conditioning inputs.
The PMI framework is demonstrated on a 3D blade design problem.
The cINN achieves significant improvements in design efficiency and accuracy.
The number of affine coupling layers used in the cINN is L.
The number of hidden layers used in the cINN is empirically determined through extensive search.
The learning rate used in the cINN is empirically determined through extensive search.
The weight decay used in the cINN is empirically determined through extensive search.
The number of epochs used in the cINN is empirically determined through extensive search.
The PMI framework is a probabilistic machine learning framework for inverse aerodynamic design of gas turbine blades.
The cINN is a conditional invertible neural network that maps design parameters to performance targets.
The forward modeling step in the PMI framework uses a probabilistic multi-fidelity Gaussian Process (MFGP) regression model.
The inverse modeling step in the PMI framework trains a cINN using data generated in the forward modeling step.
